Tenth development release of 0.19.0: PDF reports with covers, chapters, contents and sensitivity labels, a topology report, faster big lists, device ranges from device profiles and three security fixes.

> [!CAUTION]
> **This is a development release. It is not stable and it contains bugs.** Do not run it in production or on data you can't restore. Take a backup before upgrading a test install, and expect behaviour to change before 0.19.0. If you run into a problem, please [submit a bug report](https://github.com/danbyte-net/danbyte/issues/new?template=bug_report.md) - every report helps get 0.19.0 right.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Upgrade note: prefixes whose CIDR isn't an address are deleted.**
> The upgrade adds a database index that reads every prefix's CIDR as an address. A prefix holding anything else (for example `banana` or `10.0.0.0/33`) would make the index build fail and roll the whole upgrade back. To prevent that, migration `api.0265_drop_unparseable_prefixes` runs first. It deletes every prefix Postgres can't read as an address and logs each one to the upgrade log as a `danbyte.migrations` warning, with its id, value and tenant.
>
> **This is unlikely to delete anything.** A prefix should only ever hold a CIDR: Danbyte has validated prefix input since #47, and an earlier migration already turned bare addresses into host prefixes. Only junk values saved before that validation existed are affected, and those already broke prefix search and filters. If you want to be sure, take a backup before upgrading and check the upgrade log afterwards for `deleting prefix` lines.

> [!NOTE]
> **One root step after upgrading (systemd installs).** nginx now serves the frontend's build files under `/assets/` itself, cached for a year. The upgrade shows the step *Let nginx serve the frontend's build files* until root has re-rendered the site from this release's bundle. Until then everything works as before, only without the caching. If you manage nginx yourself, add the `/assets/` block and the `$danbyte_asset_cache` map from `deploy/nginx/danbyte.prod.conf.template`. Docker installs need nothing.

### PDF reports

- **Cover page** - tick *Include cover page* for a full-page title page: the deployment's logo, the tenant or project name, a title, subtitle and *Prepared by*. The background is the Danbyte waves in the tenant's colours, a plain colour, an uploaded image or none. Tenants set their colours and image under report cover settings, and a single report can pick its own cover colours.
- **Sensitivity labels** - a catalog of labels (Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted to start with, editable like statuses). Pick one in the report dialog and it prints on the cover and at the top and bottom of every page. The tenant can set a default.
- **Chapters and contents** - longer reports get chapter dividers and a clickable table of contents with page numbers, and the PDF's bookmarks follow the chapters.
- **Topology report** - pick saved views on the new `/topology` list (or *PDF report* in the map's Export menu) for one PDF with each view's diagram, its devices, IP addresses and cabling, or a ZIP with one PDF per view. The diagram pages are drawn by the same code as the map's Export ▸ PDF, so both always match.
- **#474 - Fixes** large object reports never finishing. Reports render about twice as fast, and one too big for the request now runs in the background. The dialog shows a live estimate and refuses an oversized report early, saying what fits.
- **Show IPs** - a prefix report can list each prefix's IP addresses under it.
- Prefix reports are grouped by VRF like the prefix list: Global first, a banner per VRF, children nested.
- Every time in a report and on the topology, floor plan, rack and cabinet PDFs and spec sheets is in your timezone, with the zone named, so the cover and the footer always agree.
- Report tables stay inside the page margins.

More PDF reports are coming soon, along with a dedicated reports page where you can mix different reports into one.

### New

- **Topology views list** - `/topology` now lists the saved views with who made and last changed them. The map itself moved to `/topology/map`; old links redirect with their parameters.
- **Device profiles** - a profile's page gets *Add device* (the device form with the profile filled in) and *Assign devices*, a multi-select picker that skips devices already on the profile and reports what it assigned or skipped and why.
- **Device name ranges** - the device form takes a range like `DK-RDS-[1-10]` or `[0001-0100]` and creates every device in one go, all or nothing (at most 128). Fields that belong to one device only (rack position, serial, asset tag, primary IPs) must be left blank for a range. Also available as `POST /api/devices/bulk-create/`.
- **Line type per device and per band** - in the topology Diagram a cable takes its own line type, else its ends' devices', else their bands', else the view's.
- **SBOM** - applications, platforms and installs take package URLs (purl) and CPEs, with `{version}` and `{os_version}` templates, and the SBOM writes them out. `/api/sbom/?site=` takes a site name or slug as well as an id.
- `/api/ips/` and `/api/prefixes/` filter by tag (`?tag=<slug>`, `?tag_id=<id>`).
- **Sidebar** - DCIM is regrouped into Devices, Catalog, Racks & cabinets and Connections. Applications, application groups, lifecycle, end-of-life products and support contracts move to a new **Software & lifecycle** section. Links and permissions are unchanged.

### Performance

- **#479 - Fixes** the prefix list taking 30 s with 5,000 prefixes: grouped tables are paged.
- **#482, #483, #487 - Fixes** slow Devices, Interfaces, Cables and VMs lists. They are paged, sorted, filtered and faceted on the server and only fetch the table's fields, and the 10,000-row cap is gone.
- **#480, #484 - Fixes** slow natural-order device and VM lists and prefix containment lookups with new indexes.
- **#478 - Fixes** the update check blocking workers when GitHub is slow or unreachable. The release list is cached and refreshed every 6 hours.
- **#481 - Fixes** a new database connection per request: the web workers keep theirs for 60 s (`DB_CONN_MAX_AGE`).
- **#485 - Fixes** the frontend's files being revalidated on every page load: nginx serves them, compressed and cached for a year (see the note above).
- **#486 - Fixes** a session write on every request: the idle timeout is refreshed at most once a minute, and its window starts at sign-in.
- **#488 - Fixes** several small costs: a smaller first page load, a cached import/export type list and fewer queries on the Devices page.

### Security

- **#489 - Fixes** passwords set by an admin or at bootstrap skipping the password rules. A weak password is now refused.
- **#490 - Fixes** HSTS and X-Frame-Options being sent twice with different values. nginx now owns them behind the proxy.
- **#491 - Fixes** signed-in API responses having no `Cache-Control`. They are now `private, no-store`.
- **#473 - Fixes** an interface's link peer naming a cable's far end on a site the user can't see.

### Fixed

- **#476 - Fixes** the site map on portrait phones: the objects panel no longer covers the map and the toolbar stays on screen.
- **#477 - Fixes** the cramped calendar toolbar and compliance condition rows on phones.
- **#475 - Fixes** a monitoring test that failed between 00:00 and 01:00 UTC.

### Behaviour changes

- List endpoints answer **400** for a sort column or facet they don't know, instead of ignoring it.
- A single device name with a range in it, like `x[1-3]`, is refused instead of saved as text (in the form and in CSV import).
- `/topology` is the views list; the map is at `/topology/map`.
- A weak password set by an admin is refused (#489).
